_comment: Forenames that are the SAME NAME in a different language, so the scorer can see that
Henricus and Hendrik are one man. Flanders wrote its registers in Latin until the French
period, in French under it and after it in the cities, and in Dutch elsewhere — so one
person is Joannes at his baptism, Jean at his marriage and Jan at his death, and until
this file existed those were three unrelated names to `match.py`.
It is not a small effect. Counted in the harvested corpus: joannes 183,843 + jan 92,848 +
jean 76,862 is 353,553 mentions, 8% of every person named in it. petrus + pieter + pierre
is 232,893. franciscus + frans + francois is 278,947. maria + marie is 449,453.
WHY THIS IS DATA AND NOT CODE. `match.py` holds the surname phonetic rules, and those are
regex patterns containing no names. These are names, and `data/` is the only place a name
may appear. It also means the table is greppable, diffable and correctable one line at a
time, and that a score can be explained by citing a line rather than a model.
WHY IT IS CURATED AND NOT LEARNED. Two traps, and a similarity heuristic falls into the
worse one. Measured over the obvious candidates, the Latin masculine/feminine pairs that
must NEVER fold are MORE similar than the Latin/vernacular pairs that should:
Ludovicus~Ludovica 0.82, Franciscus~Francisca 0.84, Augustinus~Augustina 0.84, against
Henricus~Hendrik 0.67, Joannes~Jan 0.60, Ludovicus~Lodewijk 0.35. The distributions are
inverted, so no threshold separates them — and the first thing a threshold reaches for is
a brother and his sister, in a tree that leans on a sex veto. The other trap is learning
pairs from confirmed matches: that equivalence would not be independent of the match that
taught it, which manufactures a second identifier out of the first and inflates confidence
on exactly the borderline pairs.
SPLIT BY SEX, AND THAT IS THE SAFETY RAIL. A masculine form can never fold to a feminine
one BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a check, because the fold only ever looks inside one
block. Ludovicus/Ludovica, Franciscus/Francisca, Joannes/Joanna, Jean/Jeanne and
Henricus/Henrica are the pairs this exists to keep apart: merging them merges a brother
with his sister, which does not look broken — it looks like one person.
THE SPLIT DOES NOT LICENSE READING SEX OFF A FORENAME. The data model forbids that
explicitly and it stays forbidden: `sex` comes from what a record says, never from a name.
These blocks decide which names may fold together and nothing else. Nothing reads them to
answer 'was this person a woman'.
RULES FOR EDITING. Tokens are normalised — lowercase, unaccented, as `normalise_key`
leaves them. A name may appear in exactly one group, in exactly one block; the validator
enforces both, and it caught the first mistake made writing this file, which was putting
`corneille` — the French masculine Cornelius — into the feminine `cornelia` group. Add a
form only when the corpus actually holds it: a group is a claim about this material, not
about onomastics in general. A folded agreement is deliberately scored below an exact one,
the same way a phonetic surname variant is.
